In a Goblin deck with Goblin Matron, Munitions Expert, Skirk Prospector, and Broadside Bombardiers, the Cavern should have been named 'Goblin' to make those creatures uncounterable. Now when tapping Cavern for colored mana (option 2), it can only be used for Shapeshifter spells, which is useless. The player should choose option 1 ({T}: Add {C}) since the colored mana from option 2 is restricted to Shapeshifters and won't help cast Munitions Expert (which costs {B}{R}). However, {C} also won't help pay for Munitions Expert's colored costs. Actually, looking more carefully - Munitions Expert is already on the stack and the player is being asked to activate Cavern of Souls to help pay for it. Option 1 produces colorless mana which doesn't help with {B}{R}. Option 2 produces colored mana but only for Shapeshifter creatures. Neither option actually helps cast Munitions Expert. The real blunder was naming Shapeshifter on Cavern of Souls instead of Goblin when it entered.

More importantly, they should play Cavern of Souls naming Goblin, then they'd have access to Mountain + Cavern (Goblin) + existing Cavern (Shapeshifter) = potentially 3 mana for Goblin Matron or Broadside Bombardiers. With Mountain providing {R}, Cavern of Souls (new, naming Goblin) providing colored mana for a Goblin, and Cavern of Souls (Shapeshifter) providing {C}, they could cast Goblin Matron (2R) using the two Caverns for colorless/colored and Mountain for R. More importantly, Aether Vial at 1 counter can put a 1-mana creature onto the battlefield - but the only 1-mana creature in hand would need to be checked. None of these are 1-mana creatures, so Aether Vial at 1 counter can't put anything into play. The pass appears correct given the hand contents. Actually, wait - Munitions Expert is 2 MV, not 1 MV. annotations.description: The player declined to activate Aether Vial, which has 1 charge counter and could put a 1-mana creature (like Munitions Expert, which is flash and costs {B}{R} but has MV 2 — wait, Munitions Expert has MV 2 not 1). Actually, Aether Vial has 1 counter and the only 1-MV creature in hand would need to match. Looking at the hand: Broadside Bombardiers (MV 3), Cavern of Souls (land), Goblin Matron (MV 3), Munitions Expert x3 (MV 2). None of these are MV 1, so Aether Vial activation wouldn't put anything onto the battlefield. However, the reasoning states 'Passing priority' without attempting anything, which is actually correct given no MV-1 creatures in hand. But the Cavern of Souls in hand hasn't been played as a land drop yet — the player should play Cavern of Souls (choosing Goblin) before passing, which would enable casting Goblin Matron (using Cavern + Mountain for the colored mana) or potentially a Munitions Expert. With Mountain + Cavern (choosing Goblin), they could cast Munitions Expert using Mountain for R and Cavern for B (as Goblin type). This would give them a creature and deal damage equal to number of Goblins controlled (Skirk Prospector + Munitions Expert = 2 damage to Ancient Tomb or the opponent's face... well, to a creature or planeswalker). The opponent has no creatures, so the ETB would have no valid target. Still, playing the land and developing the board would be better than doing nothing.

annotations.betterLine: Play Cavern of Souls (naming Goblin) as land drop, then cast Munitions Expert or Goblin Matron to develop the board. Goblin Matron would tutor for a key Goblin. Even without good ETB targets for Munitions Expert, developing the board is important.

annotations.description: The player chose to discard Atraxa, Grand Unifier but the game log shows 'GPT52 Proud discards Show and Tell' — there's a discrepancy, but analyzing the choice: with Show and Tell + Omniscience in hand (the combo), and two copies of Show and Tell, discarding a second Show and Tell is fine. However, if they actually chose Atraxa as indicated in 'Chosen', that's a significant mistake. Atraxa is the best target to put into play off Show and Tell if Omniscience isn't needed, and is a powerful follow-up after resolving Omniscience. With the Show and Tell + Omniscience combo available, casting Omniscience lets you cast everything for free — Emrakul gives an extra turn and is 15/15 with annihilator 6, but Atraxa refills your hand with up to 8 cards and is a 7/7 lifelink flyer. Discarding Atraxa removes a key payoff card. The correct discard would be one of the duplicate Ponders (less impactful when you have Omniscience about to let you cast everything) or the second Show and Tell (redundant once you resolve the first one).

annotations.betterLine: Discard a duplicate Ponder or duplicate Show and Tell instead — Atraxa is a critical payoff after resolving Omniscience via Show and Tell, providing massive card advantage and a 7/7 lifelink/deathtouch/vigilance/flying body

annotations.description: When forced to discard to hand size, the player discarded Atraxa, Grand Unifier. Aether Vial.oracle_text:
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may put a charge counter on this artifact.
{T}: You may put a creature card with mana value equal to the number of charge counters on this artifact from your hand onto the battlefield.

Ancient Tomb.oracle_text: {T}: Add {C}{C}. This land deals 2 damage to you.

Atraxa, Grand Unifier.oracle_text:
Flying, vigilance, deathtouch, lifelink
When Atraxa enters, reveal the top ten cards of your library. For each card type, you may put a card of that type from among the revealed cards into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order. (Artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, instant, land, planeswalker, and sorcery are card types.)

Broadside Bombardiers.oracle_text:
Menace, haste
Boast — Sacrifice another creature or artifact: This creature deals damage equal to 2 plus the sacrificed permanent's mana value to any target. (Activate only if this creature attacked this turn and only once each turn.)

Cavern of Souls.oracle_text:
As this land enters, choose a creature type.
{T}: Add {C}.
{T}: Add one mana of any color. Spend this mana only to cast a creature spell of the chosen type, and that spell can't be countered.

Emrakul, the Aeons Torn.oracle_text:
This spell can't be countered.
When you cast this spell, take an extra turn after this one.
Flying, protection from spells that are one or more colors, annihilator 6
When Emrakul is put into a graveyard from anywhere, its owner shuffles their graveyard into their library.

Force of Will.oracle_text:
You may pay 1 life and exile a blue card from your hand rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
Counter target spell.

Goblin Matron.oracle_text: When this creature enters, you may search your library for a Goblin card, reveal that card, put it into your hand, then shuffle.

Lotus Petal.oracle_text: {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Add one mana of any color.

Mogg War Marshal.oracle_text:
Echo {1}{R} (At the beginning of your upkeep, if this came under your control since the beginning of your last upkeep, sacrifice it unless you pay its echo cost.)
When this creature enters or dies, create a 1/1 red Goblin creature token.

Munitions Expert.oracle_text:
Flash
When this creature enters, you may have it deal damage to target creature or planeswalker equal to the number of Goblins you control.

Omniscience.oracle_text: You may cast spells from your hand without paying their mana costs.

Ponder.oracle_text:
Look at the top three cards of your library, then put them back in any order. You may shuffle.
Draw a card.

Scalding Tarn.oracle_text: {T}, Pay 1 life, Sacrifice this land: Search your library for an Island or Mountain card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

Show and Tell.oracle_text: Each player may put an artifact, creature, enchantment, or land card from their hand onto the battlefield.
